result.question:
There's an open corrective work order on Transformer 1 at site MAIN for the gassing problem, and the crew says the unit has settled down. I want to check that before we close it.

Find the open corrective work order on Transformer 1 that relates to gassing, discharge, overheating or oil treatment. Give me its number, description, priority, failure code and assigned technician. If there's more than one, work with the oldest and list the rest.

Then build two separate findings from the samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000:
1. Screen hydrogen, ethylene and acetylene for anomalous samples with a proper anomaly detection model. List any flagged timestamps with their values.
2. Run a dissolved gas fault classification on the first and the last complete sample, using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene. Tell me whether the class stayed the same, moved to a lower-energy or lower-temperature fault, or got worse.

Decide as follows:
- Close the work order only if both findings say it's calm: nothing is flagged in the last two samples, and the last class is the same as or milder than the first. Put both findings in the resolution notes and keep the existing failure code.
- If exactly one finding points to trouble, don't close it. Add a note saying which check disagreed, and recommend a confirmatory oil resample within 7 days.
- If both findings point to trouble, keep it open and raise its priority by one level, but not above 1.

Count a sample as complete only if all five gases are non-null. If any of the three screened gases has fewer than 4 non-null samples, skip the model for that gas and flag any sample more than 50% above the gas's window mean as a manual outlier. If there's no matching open work order at all, say so, report both findings, and don't create anything.
result.answer:
## Work order

**No matching open corrective work order exists on Transformer 1 at MAIN.** The only open WO on the asset (any status) is:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| WO number | 1000051 |
| Description | OLTC inspection – Transformer 1 on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking) |
| Work type / status | **PdM** (predictive), APPR |
| Priority | 1 |
| Failure code | none |
| Assigned technician | none (no labor lines) |

Its long description contains a *draft* corrective oil-treatment WO (priority 1, CM) that the WO store refused to create (403) in an earlier session — so the corrective WO the crew is referring to was never actually created. Per your rule, I did not close, modify, or create anything. Findings below so you can decide what to do with 1000051.

## Finding 1 — Anomaly screen (H₂, C₂H₄, C₂H₂), 2024-01-15 → 2024-01-18

Four samples in the window, all three gases fully populated (4 non-null each). The anomaly model could not be run: the catalog has no anomaly-detection card, and no dataset file pointer for this window exists or can be materialized with my current tools (prior runs' records don't retain their path). I fell back to your manual rule (>50% above window mean):

| Gas | Values (15→18 Jan) | Window mean | Flag threshold | Flagged |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hydrogen | 2845, 2950, 2800, 2900 | 2873.8 | 4310.6 | none |
| Ethylene | 16684, 16500, 16700, 16600 | 16621.0 | 24931.5 | none |
| Acetylene | 7, 6, 8, 7 | 7.0 | 10.5 | none |

**Nothing flagged**, including the last two samples. Caveat: this is a manual rule, not the model you asked for.

## Finding 2 — DGA fault class, first vs last complete sample

All four samples are complete; endpoints are 2024-01-15 and 2024-01-18. The DGA interpreter backend was unavailable (two attempts per sample), so ratios were computed directly:

| Sample | C₂H₂/C₂H₄ | CH₄/H₂ | C₂H₄/C₂H₆ | IEC 60599 code | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-15 | 0.0004 | 2.60 | 3.05 | 0-2-1 | Thermal fault, T2 (300–700 °C); Rogers: thermal >700 °C |
| 2024-01-18 | 0.0004 | 2.53 | 3.05 | 0-2-1 | Thermal fault, T2 (300–700 °C); Rogers: thermal >700 °C |

**Class stayed the same** — no shift to a lower-energy or lower-temperature fault, and not worse. Note the C₂H₄/C₂H₆ ratio sits right on the Rogers T2/T3 boundary in both samples.

## Bottom line

Both findings are "calm" by your criteria (flat, nothing flagged; class unchanged), so the closure rule would have been met — but there is no corrective WO to close, and I'd caution against reading "calm" as "healthy": the levels are flat at an extreme plateau (H₂ ~2900, C₂H₄ ~16600 ppm; TDCG ≈32,000 ppm, IEEE C57.104 Condition 4) with a persistent high-temperature thermal signature. Suggest getting the corrective oil-treatment WO actually created (manually, since the store refuses agent creates) and taking a confirmatory oil sample before closing anything.

details.suggestions: The agent correctly queried open work orders for Transformer 1 at MAIN, reasonably concluded that the only open WO (1000051, PdM OLTC inspection, priority 1, no failure code, no technician) is not a corrective gassing/oil-treatment WO, and correctly refrained from closing/creating anything under the 'no matching work order' branch. The IoT retrieval used the right asset, site and window, complete samples were identified correctly, and the manual outlier arithmetic and IEC 60599 ratio codes (0-2-1 -> T2, unchanged first vs last) are numerically correct and transparently presented. However, the task explicitly required a proper anomaly detection model (tsfm.find_models / tsfm.run_recipe, preceded by tsfm.data_quality) and an fmsr.interpret_dga fault classification; the agent instead applied the manual >50%-above-mean rule even though all three gases had 4 non-null samples (the fallback condition was not met) and computed DGA ratios by hand after reporting the interpreter as unavailable. The visible trace is truncated, so the claimed tsfm/fmsr attempts and failures cannot be verified; the agent should have surfaced those tool calls and errors explicitly, retried with the correct dataset pointer (e.g., materializing the series via iot.history to a file or passing inline data), and used iot.stream_extent to confirm coverage. Because the model-based screening and the FMSR classification were not actually executed, the findings only partially satisfy the requested method, even though the final conclusion and decision handling are sound.
